The 2012–13 season was [[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]'s 114th season in existence and the club's [[La Liga#All-time La Liga table|82nd consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. The season marked the managerial debut of [[Tito Vilanova]], who served as [[Pep Guardiola]]'s longtime assistant. Vilanova assumed management of the club after Guardiola, who had managed Barcelona for the prior four seasons, declined to renew his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1055344/pep-guardiola-confirms-barcelona-departure?cc=3436|title=Tito takes over after Pep.|publisher=[[ESPN Soccernet]].com|date=27 April 2012|access-date=27 April 2012|archive-date=30 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120430190648/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1055344/pep-guardiola-confirms-barcelona-departure?cc=3436|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Barcelona finished first in [[2012–13 La Liga|La Liga]] but lost in the semi-finals of both the [[2012-13 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] and the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. The club also set a record (later equaled by [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]) by scoring in all 38 La Liga matches in the season.

==Season overview==
{{cleanup|reason=needs totally rewriting - innumerable grammar errors including writing about past events in the future tense. also extreme levels of trivia, of no interest to general readers.|date=April 2025}}

===May/June===
On 29 May, Barcelona announced their first pre-season match to be against [[Hamburger SV]] in occasion of the [[Germany|German]] outfit's 125th anniversary celebration. It will be Tito Vilanova's first match in charge of the first team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-to-play-friendly-with-hamburger-sv-on-july-24|title=Barça to play friendly versus Hamburg on 24 July.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=29 May 2012|access-date=29 May 2012}}</ref> The second match will be on 28 July in [[Tangier]], [[Morocco]], versus an all-star starting XI from the [[Botola|Moroccan Football League]] at the [[Stade de Tanger]]. This will be their first appearance in Morocco in 38 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-return-to-morocco-after-38-year-break|title=Barça to play friendly versus Morocco XI.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 May 2012|access-date=30 May 2012}}</ref>

On 1 June, Barcelona announced Brazilian [[Defender (association football)|defender]] [[Henrique (footballer, born October 1986)|Henrique]] will not return to team after both agreed to terminate the player's contract on 30 June. Henrique did not make an appearance with the first team and was on-loan in [[2008–09 FC Barcelona season|2008–09]] with German club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], [[2009–10 FC Barcelona season|2009–10]], and [[2010–11 FC Barcelona season|2010–11]] with [[Racing de Santander]] and in [[2011–12 FC Barcelona season|2011–12]], with Brazilian club [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-to-end-henriques-contract|title=Henrique leaves Barça.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=1 June 2012|access-date=1 June 2012}}</ref>

On 28 June, Barcelona and [[Valencia CF]] reached an agreement on the transfer of left back [[Jordi Alba]] for €14 million. The player joined the team after [[UEFA Euro 2012]] and signed a five-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-with-valencia-over-jordi-alba|title=Jordi Alba transferred to Barcelona.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=26 June 2012|access-date=26 June 2012}}</ref>

===July===
On 7 July, Barcelona announced that [[Seydou Keita (footballer)|Seydou Keita]] would not renew his contract for the upcoming season. The [[Mali]] [[midfielder]] leaves after four years and 14 titles accumulated while at Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/keita-announces-he-wont-be-at-barca-next-season|title=Keita to depart Barça.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=7 July 2012|access-date=7 July 2012}}</ref>

On 10 July, the [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] released the fixture list for the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]], with Barcelona opening the season at [[Camp Nou]] against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/the-first-clasico-on-7th-october|title=Fixture list released.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=10 July 2012|access-date=10 July 2012}}</ref> President [[Ángel María Villar]] also confirmed that both Barcelona manager Tito Vilanova and [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] manager [[José Mourinho]] will not have to serve their suspensions in the [[2012 Supercopa de España]] for their altercation in [[2011 Supercopa de España|last year's edition]]. Barça's Board Secretary Toni Freixa stated at a press conference that an "aggression can never go unpunished" and "we understand that an aggression on a coach deserves punishment. This measure doesn't make the aggressor innocent but it allows them to believe that they can keep on being aggressive without consequences. It's a bad example for Spanish football that this aggression hasn't been punished."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/toni-freixa-the-pardon-doesnt-make-the-aggressor-innocent|title=Mourinho and Vilanova excused.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=10 July 2012|access-date=10 July 2012}}</ref>

On 13 July, Barcelona announced that the pre-season match on 28 July would be played against [[Raja Casablanca]] instead of Moroccan All-Star XI as previously announced.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/game-in-tangiers-to-be-against-raja-club-athletic|title=Tangiers match to be against Raja Club Athletic.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=13 July 2012|access-date=13 July 2012}}</ref>

On 24 July, Barcelona opened their pre-season with a 2–1 victory over Hamburg at the [[Volksparkstadion|Imtech Arena]]. Goals scored by [[Dani Alves]] and [[Gerard Deulofeu]] to set off a victorious debut for Vilanova.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/friendly/hamburg_fc-barcelona|title=Hamburg – Barcelona: Winning start for Tito (1–2)|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 July 2012|access-date=24 July 2012}}</ref> Defender [[Marc Muniesa]] left the match with a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his right knee in the 52nd minute that could possibly see him miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/marc-muniesa-serious-knee-injury|title=Muniesa seriously injured.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 July 2012|access-date=24 July 2012}}</ref> The next day, Barcelona doctors confirmed that Muniesa will miss up to six months due to the injury picked up the day before.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/marc-muniesa-out-for-six-months|title=Muniesa down for 6 months.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=25 July 2012|access-date=25 July 2012}}</ref>

On 27 July, Barcelona informed the [[Catalan Football Federation]] that [[FC Barcelona B|Barcelona B]], instead of the first team, will dispute the Supercopa de Catalunya against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] set for 31 July at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys|Olímpic Lluís Companys]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-b-to-play-for-the-catalan-super-cup|title=Barça B to dispute Supercopa de Catalunya.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 July 2012|access-date=27 July 2012}}</ref>

On 28 July, Barcelona defeated Raja Casablanca 8–0 in Tangier with [[Lionel Messi]] supplying a hat-trick while [[Alexis Sánchez]] added another two goals while Dani Alves, [[Sergi Gómez]], and Deulofeu scored one each.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/friendly/raja-club-ath-_fc-barcelona|title=Perfect performance in Tangier (0–8).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=28 July 2012|access-date=27 July 2012}}</ref>

On 30 July, Barcelona announced they accepted the rescheduled date of the Supercopa de Catalunya after the Catalan Football Association proposed the match to be played on 26 September 2012. They also stated that they would play the strongest team possible as chosen by the manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/communique-on-the-catalan-super-cup|title=Barça agree to play Supercopa.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 July 2012|access-date=30 July 2012}}</ref>

===August===
On 4 August, Barcelona defeated [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] 4–1 in penalty shoot-out after a 2–2 draw in regular time for the Trophée de Paris in [[Paris]]. [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]] and Lionel Messi scored the two goals which was kicked off by [[Eric Abidal]], who took the ceremonial kick off.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-win-paris-trophy-2-2|title=Barça win Paris Trophy (2–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=4 August 2012|access-date=4 August 2012}}</ref>

On 8 August, Barcelona defeated [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] 2–0 in a best-of-three penalty shoot-out after a 0–0 draw after regular time. [[Víctor Valdés]] saved a [[Wayne Rooney]] penalty in the first half of stoppage time, while Jordi Alba made his debut for Barcelona in the second half of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/friendly/manchester-united_fc-barcelona|title=Manchester United – Barcelona: Penalties give Barça win (0–0).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=8 August 2012|access-date=8 August 2012}}</ref>

On 11 August, Barcelona defeated [[FC Dinamo București|Dinamo București]] 2–0 with goals by Lionel Messi and [[Ibrahim Afellay]]. The two long-time injured Barça players, [[David Villa]] ([[Bone fracture|fractured]] [[tibia]]) and [[Andreu Fontàs]] (torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]]), made their returns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/friendly/d-de-bucarest_fc-barcelona/|title=Dinamo București – Barcelona: Pre-season ends with Villa and Fontàs back (0–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=11 August 2012|access-date=11 August 2012}}</ref>

On 18 August, Barcelona and [[England|English]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] reached an agreement on the transfer of [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] midfielder [[Alex Song]] for €19 million. The player signed a five-year deal with an €80 million release clause.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-with-arsenal-for-song|title=Agreement with Arsenal for Song.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=18 August 2012|access-date=18 August 2012}}</ref>

On 19 August, Barcelona started their 2012–13 La Liga season with 5–1 home win over Real Sociedad with two goals by Lionel Messi and one each by [[Carles Puyol]], [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]] and David Villa. It also marked a successful debut for Tito Vilanova's first league match as manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-1/fc-barcelona_real-sociedad|title=Barcelona – Real Sociedad: Dream start (5–1)|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 August 2012|access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref>

On 20 August, Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the season at the hands of [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] for the [[Joan Gamper Trophy]] by a score of 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/joan-gamper-trophy/fc-barcelona_sampdoria|title=Barcelona – Sampdoria: Sampdoria take Gamper (0–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 August 2012|access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref> [[Sergi Roberto]] was named the best player of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/sergi-roberto-named-mvp-of-the-joan-gamper-estrella-damm-trophy|title=Sergi Roberto named MVP with the Joan Gamper Estrella Damm Trophy.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 August 2012|access-date=20 August 2012}}</ref>

On 23 August, Barcelona defeated Real Madrid in the first leg of the Supercopa de España, 3–2, with goals by Pedro, Lionel Messi and [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]]. It was Vilanova's first game and win in a Clásico as manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/spanish-supercup/final/fc-barcelona_real-madrid|title=Barcelona – Real Madrid: Barça take control (3–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 August 2012|access-date=24 August 2012}}</ref> Messi's 14th Clásico goal allowed him to equal [[César Rodríguez Álvarez|César Rodríguez]]'s record for Barcelona and marked the first time a player scored in four consecutive Spanish Super Cup matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-equals-cesar-as-fc-barcelona-s-all-time-goalscorer-against-real-madrid|title=Messi equals César as Barcelona's all-time goalscorer.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 August 2012|access-date=24 August 2012}}</ref>

On 26 August, Barcelona came back from a 1–0 half-time deficit to defeat [[CA Osasuna]] in [[El Sadar]] with a 2–1 victory behind two goals from Lionel Messi in the last 15 minutes of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-2/osasuna_fc-barcelona|title=Barça come back to claim victory at El Sadar (1–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=26 August 2012|access-date=26 August 2012}}</ref> Carles Puyol finished with a broken cheekbone after a collision with Osasuna's [[Forward (association football)|forward]] [[Roland Lamah]] towards the end of the match,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/puyol-fractures-his-cheekbone|title=Puyol finishes match with broken cheekbone.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=26 August 2012|access-date=26 August 2012}}</ref> that also saw manager Vilanova ejected for the first time by referee [[César Muñiz Fernández|Muñiz Fernández]] for excessive argument over a play the Barça manager deemed a foul not called in favour of his team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/vilanova-praises-his-players-after-the-match-against-osasuna|title=Vilanova ejected for angrily arguing.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=26 August 2012|access-date=26 August 2012}}</ref>

On 29 August, the RFEF Competition Committee suspended manager Tito Vilanova after he was ejected in the Osasuna match for what the referee deemed as "angrily protesting a play of the match, after he had been warned by the assistant referee." Barça are set to appeal the suspension.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/club-to-appeal-tito-vilanova-s-two-match-ban|title=Vilanova suspended for 2 matches.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=29 August 2012|access-date=29 August 2012}}</ref> Later that day, Barça were defeated in the second leg of the Supercopa de España 2–1 at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] and lost the tie on away goals. Real Madrid jumped out to a 2–0 lead within the first 20 minutes and the comeback was made even tougher for Barça after the sending off of [[Adriano (footballer, born 1984)|Adriano]] in the 28th minute. Lionel Messi scored his sixth goal of the season off a free-kick and has scored in all four competitive matches to start the season for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/spanish-supercup/final/real-madrid_fc-barcelona|title=Real Madrid – Barcelona: Super Cup slips away (2–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=29 August 2012|access-date=30 August 2012}}</ref> Alex Song made his debut for Barcelona with a perfect passing statistic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/error-free-start-for-alex-song|title=Error-free start for Alex Song.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 August 2012|access-date=30 August 2012}}</ref>

On 30 August, [[UEFA]] conducted the group stage draw for the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League]] in [[Monaco]]. Barcelona were drawn into Group G along with [[Portugal|Portuguese]] club [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]] from [[Russia]], and [[2011–12 Scottish Premier League|Scottish champions]] [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/benfica-spartak-moscow-and-celtic-to-face-barca-in-the-champions-league|title=Barça drawn into Group G.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 August 2012|access-date=30 August 2012}}</ref> Barcelona [[midfielder]] [[Andrés Iniesta]] received the [[UEFA Best Player in Europe Award|2011–12 UEFA Best Player in Europe Award]], beating out teammate Lionel Messi and Real Madrid [[Forward (association football)|forward]] [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] for the prize.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/iniesta-wins-the-uefa-best-player-in-europe-award|title=Andrés Iniesta crowned Best Player in Europe by UEFA.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 August 2012|access-date=30 August 2012}}</ref>

On 31 August, Barcelona and [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] agreed on a loan of Ibrahim Afellay to the German club until 30 June 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/afellay-loaned-for-one-season-to-schalke-04|title=Afellay loaned for season to Schalke 04.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=31 August 2012|access-date=31 August 2012}}</ref>

===September===
On 2 September, Barcelona defeated Valencia 1–0 at the Camp Nou to start the league season unbeaten before the [[FIFA|FIFA international break]]. Adriano scored the lone goal in the 23rd minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-3/fc-barcelona_valencia|title=Barça stays unbeaten.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=2 September 2012|access-date=2 September 2012}}</ref>

On 12 September, Barcelona announced that midfielder Andrés Iniesta would be out 10–15 days with a pulled [[Sartorius muscle|abductor]] in his right leg which he picked up during the [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]]–[[Spain national football team|Spain]] match the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I#Georgia v Spain|day before]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/iniesta-sidelined-for-10-to-15-days|title=Iniesta sidelined for 10–15 days.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=12 September 2012|access-date=12 September 2012}}</ref>

On 15 September, Barcelona defeated [[Getafe CF]] with a scoreline of 4–1 at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]]. Lionel Messi started his first match in over a year on the bench<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/leo-messi-suplente-goleador-2205733|title=Messi plays "super sub" in win vs Getafe.|publisher=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]].es|language=es|date=15 September 2012|access-date=15 September 2012}}</ref> but came-on in the 59th minute to score two goals. David Villa added another one as he recovers to full match fitness from his fractured leg from December 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/villa-it-s-important-to-win-convincingly|title=David Villa continues progress from injury.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 September 2012|access-date=15 September 2012}}</ref> Not all was celebrations for Barça, however, as their captain, Carles Puyol, suffered a strained to the [[posterior cruciate ligament]] in his left leg in the 53rd minute. The player is expected to miss four-to-six weeks due to the knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/puyol-sidelined-for-4-to-6-weeks|title=Puyol sidelined 4–6 weeks due to knee injury.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 September 2012|access-date=15 September 2012}}</ref>

On 19 September, Barcelona made their Champions League debut for the season with a 3–2 home victory over Spartak Moscow. [[Cristian Tello]] contributed the opening goal and Lionel Messi the two winning goals, while Dani Alves scored an own goal for the visitors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/round-1-g/fc-barcelona_spartak-moscu|title=FC Barcelona-Spartak Moscow: Messi leads fightback (3–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 September 2012|access-date=19 September 2012}}</ref> Early in the first half, Barça's [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|CB]] [[Gerard Piqué]] suffered a [[sprain]]ed left foot and will be out for two to three weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/gerard-pique-to-miss-two-to-three-weeks|title=Gerard Piqué to miss two to three weeks.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 September 2012|access-date=19 September 2012}}</ref>

On 22 September, Barcelona defeated [[Granada CF|Granada]] at home 2–0 behind a goal from Xavi late in the 87th minute and an own goal in stoppage time to seal the victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-granada-saint-xavi-2-0|title=Barcelona – Granada: Xavi and Barça leave it late (2–0).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=22 September 2012|access-date=23 September 2012}}</ref>

On 28 September, Lionel Messi won his third consecutive [[Onze d'Or]] presented by the [[French language|French]] magazine ''[[Onze Mondial]]''. With 47.45% of the votes, Messi beat out Cristiano Ronaldo and [[Atlético Madrid]] forward [[Radamel Falcao]] for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/third-onze-dor-in-a-row-for-messi|title=Messi claims third consecutive Onze d'Or.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=28 September 2012|access-date=28 September 2012}}</ref>

On 29 September, Barcelona came from two goals down to claim a 3–2 victory over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium]]. After Sevilla took a 2–0 lead, two goals by [[Cesc Fàbregas]] and one by substitute David Villa in injury time kept Barça on their perfect start to the league season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-6/sevilla_fc-barcelona|title=Barça record comeback against Sevilla (2–3).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=29 September 2012|access-date=29 September 2012}}</ref> In the same match, [[Thiago Alcântara|Thiago]] picked up a knee injury that will sideline him for up to eight weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/thiago-out-for-eight-weeks|title=Thiago set to miss 8 weeks due to knee injury.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 September 2012|access-date=1 October 2012}}</ref>

===October===
On 2 October, Barcelona defeated Benfica at the [[Estádio da Luz]] with 2–0 scoreline to stay unbeaten at the top of the group. Alexis Sánchez and Cesc Fàbregas contributed the winning goals, while [[Sergio Busquets]] was sent off in the 89th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/round-2-g/benfica_fc-barcelona|title=Benfica – Barcelona: European solvency (0–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=2 October 2012|access-date=2 October 2012}}</ref> Late in the second half of the game, Carles Puyol suffered yet another injury when he landed awkwardly and dislocated his left elbow.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/puyol-dislocates-left-elbow-undergoing-tests|title=Puyol dislocates left elbow; undergoing tests.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=2 October 2012|access-date=2 October 2012}}</ref> He is expected to be out for eight weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/puyol-eight-weeks-off-from-the-pitch|title=Puyol faces eight week layoff.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=3 October 2012|access-date=3 October 2012}}</ref>

On 7 October, Barcelona drew their first game of the season with a 2–2 at home against Real Madrid. Both goals came from Lionel Messi, bringing him just one goal short of the all time [[El Clásico#All-time top scorers|Clásico scoring record]] of 18 goals by [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-7/fc-barcelona_real-madrid|title=FC Barcelona – Real Madrid: Sparkling Clásico ends all square (2–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=7 October 2012|access-date=7 October 2012}}</ref> Early in the match, Dani Alves picked up a hamstring injury in his left leg and will be out for three weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/dani-alves-out-of-action-for-three-weeks|title=Dani Alves out of action for three weeks.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=7 October 2012|access-date=7 October 2012}}</ref>

On 15 October, Barcelona announced defender Andreu Fontàs would be loan out to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/andreu-fontas-road-to-mallorca|title=Fontàs to move on loan to Mallorca.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=15 October 2012|access-date=15 October 2012}}</ref>

On 20 October, Barcelona took a wild match in [[A Coruña]], beating [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] 5–4 at the [[Estadio Riazor]]. A hat-trick by Lionel Messi gave the visitors all the hard earned three points in where they raced out to a three-goal lead within the first 20 minutes of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-8/deportivo-de-la-coruna_fc-barcelona|title=Barça conquer Riazor.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 October 2012|access-date=21 October 2012}}</ref>

On 23 October, Barcelona defeated Celtic 2–1 at home. A goal by Andrés Iniesta at the end of the first half and a Jordi Alba goal in the closing seconds helped Barcelona to take away the win<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/round-3-g/fc-barcelona_celtic/|title=FC Barcelona- Celtic Glasgow: Justice in the 94th minute (2–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=23 October 2012|access-date=23 October 2012}}</ref> in Xavi's 150th international game with Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/xavi-150-international-games-with-barca|title=Xavi, 150 international games with Barça.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=23 October 2012|access-date=23 October 2012}}</ref>

On 27 October, Barcelona defeated [[Rayo Vallecano]] with a dominating scoreline of 5–0 in [[Vallecas]]. Leo Messi scored a brace, while David Villa, Xavi and Cesc Fàbregas contributed with a goal each. This win equalled Barcelona's best start in the La Liga.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/rayo-vallecano-fc-barcelona-best-start-to-a-season-goes-on-0-5|title=Barça run wild in Vallecas.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 October 2012|access-date=29 October 2012}}</ref>

On 30 October, Barcelona started their [[2012–13 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] defence with a victory in [[Vitoria-Gasteiz]] over [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] in the first leg with a 3–0 win. Goals from David Villa, Andrés Iniesta and Cesc Fàbregas gave Barça the victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/archivo-partidos/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-16-ida/alaves_fc-barcelona|title=Barça winning debut in the Copa de Rey.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=31 October 2012|access-date=3 November 2012}}</ref>

===November===
On 3 November, Barcelona defeated [[Celta de Vigo]] 3–1 at home. With goals by Adriano, David Villa and Jordi Alba, Barça confirmed their best start in La Liga in club history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-10/fc-barcelona_celta-de-vigo|title=FC Barcelona – Celta: Win marks record breaking start (3–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=3 November 2012|access-date=3 November 2012}}</ref> Adriano had to leave the game early with a muscle tear in his right thigh and will be out of action for three weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/adriano-out-of-action-for-three-weeks|title=Adriano out of action for three weeks.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=3 November 2012|access-date=3 November 2012}}</ref>
The win opened a three-point gap at the top of the league over [[Atlético Madrid]].

On 7 November, Barcelona suffered their first Champions League loss of the season with a [[Celtic F.C. 2–1 FC Barcelona|2–1 loss]] in [[Glasgow]] against Celtic. The lone goal by Lionel Messi came in the closing minutes of the game. This loss marked Barça's first away defeat in the Champions League Group Stage since 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/round-4-g/celtic_fc-barcelona|title=Celtic – FC Barcelona: Squandered opportunity (2–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=7 November 2012|access-date=8 November 2012}}</ref>

On 11 November, Barcelona defeated Mallorca 4–2 at the [[Iberostar Stadium|Iberostar]]. Goals by Xavi, Cristian Tello and a brace by Lionel Messi helped equalizing the best ever La Liga start after the first 11 games of the season, previously archived by Real Madrid [[1968–69 La Liga|1968–69]] and [[1991–92 La Liga|1991–92]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-11/mallorca_fc-barcelona|title=R.Mallorca-FC Barcelona: Messi stalls Mallorca fightback (2–4).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=11 November 2012|access-date=11 November 2012}}</ref> With 76 goals to his name in 2012, Messi also overtook [[Pelé]]'s record of 75 goals in a single calendar year from 1958 and is only nine goals from drawing with the all-time record from 1972 by [[Gerd Müller]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/o-rei-messi-surpasses-pele|title=O Rei Messi surpasses Pelé.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=11 November 2012|access-date=11 November 2012}}</ref>

On 16 November, Barcelona announced that [[Qatar Airways]] will be the new [[shirt sponsor]] starting the [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|2013–14 season]], marking the first official [[Advertising|commercial]] sponsor on the Barcelona shirt in team's history. President [[Sandro Rosell]] stated "(Qatar Airways) an ambitious brand with global aspirations, always committed to achieving the utmost excellence in its field. These are objectives with which FC Barcelona fully identifies."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/qatar-airways-shirt-season-2013-2014|title=Barça make first commercial shirt sponsor official.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=16 November 2012|access-date=17 November 2012}}</ref>

On 17 November, Barcelona defeated [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] with 3–1 at home with another brace by Lionel Messi and [[Alex Song]]'s first goal for Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-12/fc-barcelona_saragossa|title=FC Barcelona – Zaragoza: Three more goals and three more points.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=17 November 2012|access-date=19 November 2012}}</ref>

On 18 November, Marc Bartra pulled the adductor in his right leg during a training session and will be sidelined for 15–20 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/marc-bartra-sidelined-for-15-to-20-days|title=Marc Bartra sidelined for 15 to 20 days.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=18 November 2012|access-date=19 November 2012}}</ref>

On 20 November, Barcelona defeated Spartak Moscow at the [[Luzhniki Stadium]] 3–0. One goal by Dani Alves and two by Lionel Messi helped Barça to qualify for the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]] of the Champions League with one game left to play.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/round-5-g/spartak-moscu_fc-barcelona|title=Spartak Moskow – FC Barcelona: Unstoppable Barça into last sixteen (0–3).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 November 2012|access-date=20 November 2012}}</ref>

On 25 November, Barcelona defeated [[Levante UD|Levante]] in the [[Estadi Ciutat de València|Ciutat de València]] 4–0. A brace by Lionel Messi and one goal each by Cesc Fàbregas and Andrés Iniesta, the latter also contributing three assists, as well as a penalty save by [[Víctor Valdés]] kept Barça on top of La Liga. For over 60 minutes Barcelona played with only [[La Masia]] graduates, after Dani Alves came off injured after 13 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-13/llevant_fc-barcelona|title=Levante – FC Barcelona: Masia alumni put four past Levante.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=25 November 2012|access-date=25 November 2012}}</ref>

On 28 November, Barcelona defeated Alavés with 3–1 at home. One goal by Adriano and two by David Villa helped Barça to advance to the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey#Round of 16|Round of 16]] of the Copa del Rey, where they will face [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-16-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_alaves|title=FC Barcelona – Alavés: Comeback and into last sixteen.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=28 November 2012|access-date=28 November 2012}}</ref> With the brace, David Villa passed the 300 career goals mark to 301 goals as a professional, including club and country, Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/david-villa-passes-the-300-goal-mark|title=Villa reaches 300 professional goals.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=28 November 2012|access-date=29 November 2012}}</ref>

On 29 November, [[FIFA]] announced the three finalists for the [[2012 FIFA Ballon d'Or]] to be presented on 7 January 2013: Lionel Messi and Andrés Iniesta from Barcelona and Cristiano Ronaldo from Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1959407/index.html?intcmp=newsreader_news_caption|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130031609/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/news/newsid=1959407/index.html?intcmp=newsreader_news_caption|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 November 2012|title=Ballon d'Or finalist announced.|publisher=[[FIFA]].com|date=29 November 2012|access-date=29 November 2012}}</ref> This marks the third season in a row that at least two finalist are from Barcelona and the six year in a row that Messi makes the final three.

===December===
On 1 December, Barcelona defeated [[Athletic Bilbao]] 5–1 at home with two goals by Lionel Messi and one each by Gerard Piqué, Adriano, and Cesc Fàbregas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-14/fc-barcelona_athletic-club|title=FC Barcelona – Athletic Club: Classic performance (5–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=1 December 2012|access-date=1 December 2012}}</ref> With this win Barça set up the best ever start of any team in La Liga.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-seal-best-ever-start-in-the-history-of-la-liga|title=Barça seal best ever start in the history of La Liga.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=1 December 2012|access-date=1 December 2012}}</ref> Messi's two goals made him equalize with César Rodríguez as Barcelona's [[List of FC Barcelona records and statistics#La Liga|top scorers in La Liga]] with 190 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-equals-cesars-record|title=Messi equals César's record.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=2 December 2012|access-date=2 December 2012}}</ref>

On 5 December, Barcelona played their first goalless game of the season, drawing 0–0 against Benfica at home. Shortly after coming on, Lionel Messi had to be carried off on a stretcher after twisting his knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/round-6-g/fc-barcelona_benfica|title=FC Barcelona – Benfica: Frozen (0–0).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=5 December 2012|access-date=5 December 2012}}</ref> It was later revealed that Messi picked up a contusion on the outside of his left knee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-es-retira-en-llitera|title=Messi is carted off the pitch after sustaining a contusion on his left knee.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=6 December 2012|access-date=6 December 2012}}</ref>

On 9 December, Barcelona defeated [[Real Betis]] in the [[Estadio Benito Villamarín|Benito Villamarín]] 2–1. With two more goals by Lionel Messi, Barça continued their undefeated run in away games to start La Liga season to eight matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-15/betis_fc-barcelona|title=Betis – FC Barcelona: No limits (1–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=9 December 2012|access-date=9 December 2012}}</ref> Those goals also sent Messi's tally to 86 in 2012, overtaking [[Germans|German]] [[Forward (association football)|striker]] [[Gerd Müller]]'s record of 85 goals in a calendar year in 1972.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-breaks-muller-s-record-of-goals-scored-in-a-calendar-year|title=Messi breaks Müller's record of goals scored in a calendar year.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=9 December 2012|access-date=9 December 2012}}</ref> Early in the game, Cesc Fàbregas was subbed off with a torn [[Biceps femoris muscle|biceps femoris]] in his left thigh and will be sidelined for three-to-four weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/cesc-to-miss-three-to-four-weeks|title=Cesc to miss three to four weeks.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=9 December 2012|access-date=9 December 2012}}</ref>

On 12 December, Barcelona defeated Córdoba at the [[Estadio Nuevo Arcángel|Nuevo Arcángel]] 2–0. Both goals were scored by Lionel Messi in his first Copa del Rey game of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-8-1st-leg/cordoba_fc-barcelona|title=Córdoba – FC Barcelona: On course for the quarters (0–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=12 December 2012|access-date=12 December 2012}}</ref>

On 16 December, Barcelona defeated [[Atlético Madrid]] at home 4–1. Two goals by Lionel Messi and one each by Adriano and [[Sergio Busquets]]. This victory helped Barça to draw nine points clear at the top of the table, and Messi's goals brought his record up to 90 for the year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-16/fc-barcelona_at-madrid|title=FC Barcelona – Atlético de Madrid: Leaders throw down the gauntlet (4–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=16 December 2012|access-date=16 December 2012}}</ref>

On 17 December, Cristian Tello extended his contract with Barcelona until 30 June 2016, with a set buyout clause of €10 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/tello-signs-his-new-contract|title=Cristian Tello signs through 2016.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=17 December 2012|access-date=17 December 2012}}</ref>

On 18 December, Barcelona announced the renewal of contracts with Carles Puyol and Xavi until 2016 and Lionel Messi until 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/carles-puyol-xavi-hernandez-and-leo-messi-renew-their-contract-with-fc-barcelona|title=Barça has renewed the contracts of Carles Puyol, Xavi Hernández and Leo Messi.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=18 December 2012|access-date=18 December 2012}}</ref>

On 19 December, Barcelona's Medical Services announced that manager Tito Vilanova was to undergo surgery on the following day after a routine check-up revealed that he suffered a [[parotid gland|parotid]] ailment relapse, which he was operated on a [[2011–12 FC Barcelona season#November|year previous]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/tito-vilanova-to-undergo-surgery-this-thursday|title=Tito Vilanova to undergo surgery this Thursday.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 December 2012|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref> During the recovery time, assistant coach [[Jordi Roura]] will lead Barça.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/roura-to-lead-barca-in-tito-vilanova-s-absence|title=Roura to lead Barça in Tito Vilanova's absence.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 December 2012|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref>

On 20 December, [[UEFA]] conducted the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|Round of 16]] draw for the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League]] in [[Nyon]]. Barcelona were drawn to face [[Italy|Italian]] club [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], who they last faced in the previous season's [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/next-champions-league-rival-ac-milan|title=AC Milan, The Next Champions League rival.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 December 2012|access-date=20 December 2012}}</ref>

On 22 December, Barcelona won their last match of the year at the [[Estadio Nuevo José Zorrilla|José Zorrilla]] against [[Real Valladolid]] with a score of 3–1. Goals by Xavi, Lionel Messi and Cristian Tello helped to keep the nine point lead on top of the table intact.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-17/valladolid_fc-barcelona|title=R.Valladolid – FC Barcelona: Courage and football (1–3).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=22 December 2012|access-date=22 December 2012}}</ref>

On 23 December, Barcelona announced that backup goalkeeper [[José Manuel Pinto]] came to an agreement with the club to extend his contract for another year until 30 June 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-to-extend-pinto-contract-to-june-30-2014|title=Agreement to extend Pinto contract to June 30, 2014.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=23 December 2012|access-date=23 December 2012}}</ref>

===January===
On 6 January, Barcelona won their first match of the year at home, against Espanyol 4–0. Two goals by Pedro and one each by Xavi and Lionel Messi were scored in the first 30 minutes of the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-18/fc-barcelona_espanyol|title=FC Barcelona – Espanyol: Kings of football! (4–0).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=6 January 2013|access-date=6 January 2013}}</ref>

On 7 January, Lionel Messi was announced the [[2012 FIFA Ballon d'Or]] winner in [[Zürich]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/playeroftheyear/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111022033859/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/playeroftheyear/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 October 2011|title=Messi win's 4th straight Ballon d'Or.|publisher=[[FIFA]].com|date=7 January 2013|access-date=9 January 2013}}</ref> With 41.60% of the votes, Messi became the first player to win the award on four occasions, surpassing [[Johan Cruyff]], [[Michel Platini]] and [[Marco van Basten]], all with three. The win also gave Barcelona its tenth winner, the most all time of any European club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-the-club-with-ten-ballons-dor|title=Barça claims its 10th Ballon d'Or with Messi's win.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=8 January 2013|access-date=9 January 2013}}</ref> Barcelona also celebrated five players in the [[FIFPro#FIFA FIFPro World XI|2012 FIFA FIFPro World XI]], as Messi was joined by teammates Gerard Piqué, Dani Alves, Andrés Iniesta and Xavi as the world's best for 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/world11/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101031140958/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/world11/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 October 2010|title=5 Barça players in the 2012 FIFA FIFPro World XI.|publisher=[[FIFA]].com|date=7 January 2013|access-date=9 January 2013}}</ref>

On 10 January, Barcelona beat Córdoba in the return leg of the Copa del Rey at home by 5–0, with one goal scored by Thiago and two each by David Villa and Alexis Sánchez. With an aggregate score of 7–0, Barça went through to the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]], where they will face [[Málaga CF|Málaga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-8-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_cordoba|title=FC Barcelona v Cordoba: Five goal display to reach quarter finals (5–0).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=10 January 2013|access-date=10 January 2013}}</ref> Early in the second half of the game, [[Sergi Roberto]] was subbed off with a tear in his left [[hamstring]] and will be out of action for four weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/sergi-roberto-out-of-action-for-four-weeks|title=Sergi Roberto out of action for four weeks.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=10 January 2013|access-date=10 January 2013}}</ref>

On 13 January, Barcelona beat Málaga at the [[La Rosaleda Stadium]] 3–1, with goals by Lionel Messi, Cesc Fàbregas and Thiago. With this win, Barça ended the first round of the season with a record-breaking 55 out of a possible 57 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-19/malaga_fc-barcelona|title=Málaga – FC Barcelona: Win marks historic start to season.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=13 January 2013|access-date=13 January 2013}}</ref>

On 16 January, Barcelona drew 2–2 against Málaga at home in the first leg of the Copa del Rey quarter-finals. Goals by Lionel Messi and Carles Puyol were scored within one minute of each other.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-4-1st-leg/fc-barcelona_malaga|title=FC Barcelona – Málaga: All to be decided (2–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=16 January 2013|access-date=16 January 2013}}</ref>

On 18 January, Barcelona announced that goalkeeper Víctor Valdés will not be extending his contract any further after his current contract expires on 30 June 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/zubizarreta-we-respect-valdes-professional-and-irrevocable-decision|title=Zubizarreta: "We respect Valdés' professional and irrevocable decision".|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=18 January 2013|access-date=18 January 2013}}</ref>

On 19 January, Barcelona lost their first league game away against [[Real Sociedad]] at the [[Anoeta Stadium]], 3–2. After leading by two goals from Messi and Pedro, Gerard Piqué was sent off with a second yellow and Sociedad turned the game around and scored the winning goal in the dying minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-20/real-sociedad_fc-barcelona|title=Reial Societat-FC Barcelona: Unbeaten run ends at Anoeta (3–2).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=19 January 2013|access-date=19 January 2013}}</ref>

On 24 January, Barcelona defeated Málaga in the La Rosaleda 4–2, with goals by Pedro, Piqué, Iniesta and Messi. With an aggregate score of 6–4, Barça went through to the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey#Semi-finals|Copa del Rey semi-finals]], where they will face Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-4-2nd-leg/malaga_fc-barcelona|title=Málaga – FC Barcelona: They never let us down (2–4).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=24 January 2013|access-date=24 January 2013}}</ref>

On 27 January, Barcelona defeated Osasuna at home 5–1 with four goals by Messi and one from Pedro.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-21/fc-barcelona_osasuna|title=FCB-Osasuna: Messi leads Barça to impressive win.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 January 2013|access-date=27 January 2013}}</ref> With those goals, Messi broke the 200-goal barrier in La Liga, becoming the youngest player to archive that feat at just 25 years and 217 days of age.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/leo-messi-breaks-the-200-goal-barrier-in-la-liga|title=Leo Messi breaks the 200-goal barrier in La Liga.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=27 January 2013|access-date=27 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/blog/_/name/fiveaside/id/453?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216033026/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/blog/_/name/fiveaside/id/453?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 February 2013|title=5 notes on Messi's milestone.|work=ESPN.com|date=27 January 2013|access-date=27 January 2013}}</ref>

On 30 January, Barcelona drew 1–1 against Real Madrid in the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] in the first leg of the Copa del Rey semi-finals. The lone Barça goal was scored by Cesc Fàbregas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-2-1st-leg/real-madrid_fc-barcelona|title=R.Madrid-FCB: Barça draw but deserve much more.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=30 January 2013|access-date=30 January 2013}}</ref>

On 31 January, Barcelona and [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] agreed on the loan of forward [[Isaac Cuenca]] to the Dutch club until 30 June 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/isaac-cuenca-to-join-ajax-on-loan-through-june-30|title=Isaac Cuenca to join Ajax on loan through June 30.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=31 January 2013|access-date=31 January 2013}}</ref> On the same day, Barça announced that defender [[Marc Muniesa]] will join the [[FC Barcelona B|B team]] for the rest of the season after having recovered from a torn [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/barca-enroll-marc-muniesa-in-barca-b-squad-set-to-wear-the-number-21|title=Barça enroll Marc Muniesa in Barça B squad; set to wear the number 21.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=31 January 2013|access-date=31 January 2013}}</ref>

===February===
On 3 February, Barcelona drew their second league match of the season and their second season match in a row. A 1–1 draw against Valencia at the [[Mestalla Stadium]] saw Messi scoring the only goal through a penalty.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-22/valencia_fc-barcelona|title=Valencia – FC Barcelona: Valuable point at Mestalla (1–1).|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=3 February 2013|access-date=3 February 2013}}</ref> Xavi, who was substituted in injury time of the match, was diagnosed the following day with a hamstring injury and will be sidelined for 15 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/xavi-hernandez-out-for-15-days|title=Xavi Hernández out for 15 days.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=4 February 2013|access-date=4 February 2013}}</ref> Barcelona faced Milan in the first leg of the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|Champions League round of 16]] at the [[San Siro]] and lost 2–0, with goals coming from [[Kevin-Prince Boateng]] and [[Sulley Muntari]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/ac-milan-fc-barcelona-magic-needed-at-the-camp-nou-2-0|title=AC Milan – FC Barcelona: Magic needed at the Camp Nou (2–0)|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=20 February 2013|access-date=21 February 2013}}</ref>

On 21 February, Barcelona announced that defender Eric Abidal is fit to play for the first time since receiving a liver transplant in April 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.ndtv.com/football/news/item/203983-eric-abidal-fit-for-barcelona-after-liver-transplant|title=Eric Abidal fit for Barcelona after liver transplant|agency=Associated Press|date=21 February 2013|work=NDTVSports.com|access-date=23 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130224034932/http://sports.ndtv.com/football/news/item/203983-eric-abidal-fit-for-barcelona-after-liver-transplant|archive-date=24 February 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 24 February, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 2–1 at Camp Nou with goals from David Villa and Lionel Messi.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/match/85474/barcelona-vs-sevilla/report|title=Barcelona 2 - 1 Sevilla Match report - 24/02/13 Primera División - Goal.com|work=goal.com}}</ref> On 26 February, Barcelona were defeated by Real Madrid 3–1, 4–2 on aggregate, at the Camp Nou and were knocked out of Copa del Rey contention.
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/copa-del-rey/1-2-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_real-madrid|title=FC Barcelona – Real Madrid CF|work=fcbarcelona.com}}</ref>

===March===
On 2 March, Barcelona lost to Real Madrid at the Santiago Bernabéu by a score of 2–1. This was Barcelona's second loss against Real Madrid in a week. Four days later, Víctor Valdés was handed a four-match league ban after receiving a double yellow card for verbally abusing a referee following his team's defeat in the ''Clásico'' in the weekend fixture.<ref>{{cite news|title=Victor Valdes Suspension|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/mar/06/barcelona-victor-valdes-ban-red-card|publisher=Guardian|access-date=6 March 2013|location=London|date=6 March 2013}}</ref>

On 9 March, Barcelona defeated Deportivo de La Coruña 2–0 with goals from Alexis Sánchez and Lionel Messi.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-deportivo-big-step-forward-in-the-league-2-0|title=FC Barcelona – Deportivo: Big step forward in the league (2–0)|work=fcbarcelona.com}}</ref> On 12 March, Barcelona defeated Milan 4–0, 4–2 on aggregate, and entered the quarter-finals of the Champions League with goals from David Villa, Jordi Alba and a brace from Lionel Messi.<ref>{{cite web|title=Round Of 16|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1564682-barcelona-4-0-milan-messi-and-co-at-their-brilliant-best-in-unforgettable-game|publisher=Goal.com|access-date=13 March 2013}}</ref> On 17 March, Barcelona defeated Rayo Vallecano 3–1 at Camp Nou with Messi scoring two and Villa scoring one goal.<ref>{{cite web|title=17 March|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-28/fc-barcelona_rayo-vallecano|publisher=FC Barcelona}}</ref> On 30 March, Barça drew 2–2 with Celta de Vigo with Messi and Cristian Tello scoring one goal each.<ref>{{cite web|title=30 March|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/1-4-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_psg|publisher=FCB}}</ref>

===April===
On 2 April, Barça drew 2–2 against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in France in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final, the goals coming from Messi and Xavi via a penalty.<ref>{{cite web|title=P.S.G|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/facts-and-figures-from-the-paris-game}}</ref>

On 10 April, Barça drew 1–1 against PSG at home in the Camp Nou in the Champions League quarter-final second leg. Pedro scored the all-important equaliser, which put Barça through to the semi-finals on the away goals rule.<ref>{{cite web|title=FCB vs PSG|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/champions-league/1-4-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_psg}}</ref> The draw for the semi-finals of the Champions League was held on 12 April, with Barça drawing with [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Uefa Semis| date=12 April 2013 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0208-0e9f4df5d7a3-6b609eec6dd7-1000--uefa-champions-league-semi-final-draw/|publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

On 14 April, Barcelona defeated Zarozoga 3–0 away from home.
<ref>{{cite web|title=14 April|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2012-2013/league/round-31/saragossa_fc-barcelona/stats|publisher=FC Barcelona|access-date=15 April 2013}}</ref> A 1–0 win over Levante on 20 April means that Barcelona need a maximum of six more points to secure the 2012–13 La Liga title.

On 23 April, Barcelona lost to Bayern 4–0 away at the [[Allianz Arena]] in [[Munich]], their largest defeat in Europe in 16 years. On 1 May, in the second leg at home, they lost 3–0. With an aggregate score of 7–0, they were knocked out of the Champions League in the semi-finals.

===May===
On 5 May, Barcelona defeated Real Betis 4–2 at home with two goals by Lionel Messi and one each by David Villa and Alexis Sánchez with one more win to secure the La Liga title.

On 11 May, Barcelona clinched their 22nd La Liga title after Real Madrid's draw against Espanyol at the [[RCDE Stadium|Cornellà-El Prat]]. The result gave Barcelona an eight-point lead with two matches remaining, which ensured that they would finish top of the table. Barcelona were at the top of the league table for the entirety of the season, and only lost two matches en route to winning the title. It was the first title for manager Vilanova.

On 30 May, French defender Eric Abidal called a press conference to announce his departure from the club after six seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/all-details-about-the-abidal-s-press-conference |title=Abidal's Press Conference|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 May 2013 |access-date=30 May 2013}}</ref> Although admitting he wanted to see out his career as a Barça player, the club ultimately decided not to renew his contract.

===Fair Play award===
This award is given annually since 1999 to the team with the best fair play during the season. This ranking takes into account aspects such as cards, suspension of matches, audience behaviour and other penalties. This section not only aims to determine the best fair play, but also serves to break the tie in teams that are tied in all the other rules: points, head-to-head, goal difference and goals scored.
